_game: ViZDoom: Take Cover (Doom dodging; COOM engine)
_note: pip install vizdoom. Fireball-dodging: monsters on the far wall shoot at you and more of them spawn over time, and all you can do is strafe. Reward is one point per tic survived; there is no weapon and no attack button.
_keys_note: Action indices are scenario-specific. For VizdoomTakeCover-v1 the Discrete(3) map is 0=noop, 1=MOVE_RIGHT, 2=MOVE_LEFT (verify with env.unwrapped.button_map). The adapter puts strafing on Z/X; since this scenario cannot turn, 'keys' below also points the LEFT/RIGHT arrows at the same two buttons, so both pairs work. 'keys' are always these Discrete indices; env_kwargs.max_buttons_pressed picks how held keys combine: 0 = MultiBinary (keys OR together), 1 = Discrete (one key wins). The controls the subject sees are a plain 'message' phase; keep its text in sync with 'keys' by hand.
_audio_note: env_kwargs.audio_buffer_enabled turns Doom's sound on: it arrives in obs['audio'], is played through the session's speakers, and is logged per frame. Doom makes 1/35 s of sound per step, so fps * env_kwargs.frame_skip must be 35: the session stops the block otherwise, because sound could not follow the frames.
